patch.objective: Troubleshooting software: OS errors, application issues, and patching failures

sources.cite: CompTIA Server+ SK0-005 (V5) Exam Objectives, document version 7.0: Hardware 18%, Server Administration 30%, Security and Disaster Recovery 24%, Troubleshooting 28%
sources.note: Read 2026-11-17 through a summarizing fetch of CompTIA's PDF. Relevant text: 'Given a scenario, configure servers to use network infrastructure services' (name resolution, DNS); 'Explain the key concepts of high availability for servers' (load balancing); 'Given a scenario, configure and maintain server functions and features' (monitoring, performance: CPU); 'Given a scenario, troubleshoot common OS and software problems' (service failures; services and processes); 'Explain the importance of backups and restores' (backup validation); 'Explain important concepts pertaining to identity and access management for server administration' (user groups; permissions). The objective wording here is the course seed's.

Relevant text: Restart=, 'If set to no (the default), the service will not be restarted'; 'If set to on-failure, the service will be restarted when the process exits with a non-zero exit code', and on an unclean signal; RestartSec= 'Defaults to 100ms'; 'service restart is subject to unit start rate limiting configured with StartLimitIntervalSec= and StartLimitBurst='. Read through a summarizing fetch 2026-11-14.

Relevant text: systemd.unit(5), 'Along with a unit file foo.service, a "drop-in" directory foo.service.d/ may exist. All files with the suffix ".conf" from this directory will be merged'; 'Drop-in files in /etc/ take precedence over those in /run/ which in turn take precedence over those in /usr/lib/'; /usr/lib/systemd/system holds 'System units installed by the distribution package manager'. systemctl(1), edit: 'Otherwise, a drop-in file will be created or edited' (default name override.conf) and 'After the editing is finished, configuration is reloaded, equivalent to systemctl daemon-reload'; daemon-reload 'reload all unit files'; cat may not match 'the system manager's understanding' if files changed without daemon-reload. Read through summarizing fetches 2026-11-14. That a package upgrade replaces its own file under /usr/lib is how package managers treat files that are not configuration files (dpkg(1) conffile handling, read 2026-11-14); the warning text after an unreloaded change is authored in systemd's style.
